public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Collatz step differences

Differences in adjacent elements of the sequence quantifying the steps needed for $n$ to
converge to 1 in the Collatz Conjecture.
$$a(n) = \mathrm{A006577}(n+1) - \mathrm{A006577}(n)$$
for $n > 0$.

*References:*
- [A153330](https://oeis.org/A153330)-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA153330

/-- Single step of the Collatz mapping. -/
def collatzStep (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if n % 2 = 0 then n / 2 else 3 * n + 1

open Classical in
/-- Number of iterations required to turn $n$ into 1 in the Collatz process,
or `none` if $n$ does not terminate. -/
noncomputable def collatzSteps (n : ℕ) : Option ℕ :=
  if n = 0 then none
  else if ∃ k : ℕ, (collatzStep^[k]) n = 1 then
    some (sInf {k : ℕ | (collatzStep^[k]) n = 1})
  else
    none

open Classical in
/-- The sequence $a(n) = \mathrm{A006577}(n+1) - \mathrm{A006577}(n)$ for $n > 0$,
or `none` if either $n$ or $n+1$ does not terminate. -/
noncomputable def a (n : ℕ) : Option ℤ :=
  if n = 0 then none
  else
    match collatzSteps (n + 1), collatzSteps n with
    | some s2, some s1 => some (s2 - s1)
    | _, _ => none

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 0. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = none := by rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 1. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = some 1 := by
  have h1 : IsLeast {k : ℕ | (collatzStep^[k]) 1 = 1} 0 := ⟨rfl, by simp [lowerBounds]⟩
  have h2 : IsLeast {k : ℕ | (collatzStep^[k]) 2 = 1} 1 := by
    constructor
    · rfl
    · intro k hk; by_contra! h; interval_cases k; revert hk; decide
  have hs1 : collatzSteps 1 = some 0 := by
    have h : ∃ k, (collatzStep^[k]) 1 = 1 := ⟨0, h1.1⟩
    rw [collatzSteps, if_neg (by omega), if_pos h, h1.csInf_eq]
  have hs2 : collatzSteps 2 = some 1 := by
    have h : ∃ k, (collatzStep^[k]) 2 = 1 := ⟨1, h2.1⟩
    rw [collatzSteps, if_neg (by omega), if_pos h, h2.csInf_eq]
  rw [a, if_neg (by omega), hs2, hs1]; rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = some 6 := by
  have h2 : IsLeast {k : ℕ | (collatzStep^[k]) 2 = 1} 1 := by
    constructor
    · rfl
    · intro k hk; by_contra! h; interval_cases k; revert hk; decide
  have h3 : IsLeast {k : ℕ | (collatzStep^[k]) 3 = 1} 7 := by
    constructor
    · rfl
    · intro k hk; by_contra! h; interval_cases k <;> revert hk <;> decide
  have hs2 : collatzSteps 2 = some 1 := by
    have h : ∃ k, (collatzStep^[k]) 2 = 1 := ⟨1, h2.1⟩
    rw [collatzSteps, if_neg (by omega), if_pos h, h2.csInf_eq]
  have hs3 : collatzSteps 3 = some 7 := by
    have h : ∃ k, (collatzStep^[k]) 3 = 1 := ⟨7, h3.1⟩
    rw [collatzSteps, if_neg (by omega), if_pos h, h3.csInf_eq]
  rw [a, if_neg (by omega), hs3, hs2]; rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 3. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = some (-5) := by
  have h3 : IsLeast {k : ℕ | (collatzStep^[k]) 3 = 1} 7 := by
    constructor
    · rfl
    · intro k hk; by_contra! h; interval_cases k <;> revert hk <;> decide
  have h4 : IsLeast {k : ℕ | (collatzStep^[k]) 4 = 1} 2 := by
    constructor
    · rfl
    · intro k hk; by_contra! h; interval_cases k <;> revert hk <;> decide
  have hs3 : collatzSteps 3 = some 7 := by
    have h : ∃ k, (collatzStep^[k]) 3 = 1 := ⟨7, h3.1⟩
    rw [collatzSteps, if_neg (by omega), if_pos h, h3.csInf_eq]
  have hs4 : collatzSteps 4 = some 2 := by
    have h : ∃ k, (collatzStep^[k]) 4 = 1 := ⟨2, h4.1⟩
    rw [collatzSteps, if_neg (by omega), if_pos h, h4.csInf_eq]
  rw [a, if_neg (by omega), hs4, hs3]; rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 4. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = some 3 := by
  have h4 : IsLeast {k : ℕ | (collatzStep^[k]) 4 = 1} 2 := by
    constructor
    · rfl
    · intro k hk; by_contra! h; interval_cases k <;> revert hk <;> decide
  have h5 : IsLeast {k : ℕ | (collatzStep^[k]) 5 = 1} 5 := by
    constructor
    · rfl
    · intro k hk; by_contra! h; interval_cases k <;> revert hk <;> decide
  have hs4 : collatzSteps 4 = some 2 := by
    have h : ∃ k, (collatzStep^[k]) 4 = 1 := ⟨2, h4.1⟩
    rw [collatzSteps, if_neg (by omega), if_pos h, h4.csInf_eq]
  have hs5 : collatzSteps 5 = some 5 := by
    have h : ∃ k, (collatzStep^[k]) 5 = 1 := ⟨5, h5.1⟩
    rw [collatzSteps, if_neg (by omega), if_pos h, h5.csInf_eq]
  rw [a, if_neg (by omega), hs5, hs4]; rfl

/-- The set of positive indices $n$ for which $a(n) = v$. -/
def indices (v : ℤ) : Set ℕ :=
  {n : ℕ | 0 < n ∧ a n = some v}

/--
Conjecture 1: More than half of the terms are 0.
- _Ya-Ping Lu_, May 04 2024
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture1 :
    1 / 2 < Filter.atTop.liminf (fun n : ℕ ↦
      (((Finset.Icc 1 n).filter (fun i ↦ a i = some 0)).card : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Conjecture 2: 1, 6 and 16 appear only once and 3 appears twice in the sequence,
i.e., $a(1) = 1$, $a(2) = 6$, $a(4) = a(5) = 3$, and $a(8) = 16$.
- _Ya-Ping Lu_, May 04 2024
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture2 :
    indices 1 = {1} ∧
    indices 6 = {2} ∧
    indices 16 = {8} ∧
    indices 3 = {4, 5} := by
  sorry

/--
Conjecture 3 (Ya-Ping Lu, 2024):
Except 1, 3 and 6, the absolute value of all terms can be written as $5x + 8y$ for $x, y \in \mathbb{N}$.
(Note: in the OEIS comment, "x and y are integers" means $x$ and $y$ have the same sign,
i.e., $|v| = 5x + 8y$ with $x, y \ge 0$, since every integer is a $\mathbb{Z}$-linear combination of 5 and 8).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture3 (n : ℕ) (v : ℤ) (hn : 0 < n) (ha : a n = some v)
    (hv : v ≠ 1 ∧ v ≠ 3 ∧ v ≠ 6) :
    ∃ x y : ℕ, v.natAbs = 5 * x + 8 * y := by
  sorry

/--
Conjecture 4 (Ya-Ping Lu, 2024):
The ratio of the number of terms with value $m$ to that of $-m$ approaches 1 as $n \to \infty$,
for any $m \notin \{1, 3, 6, 16\}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture4 (m : ℤ) (hm : m ≠ 1 ∧ m ≠ 3 ∧ m ≠ 6 ∧ m ≠ 16) :
    Filter.atTop.Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ ↦
        (((Finset.Icc 1 n).filter (fun i ↦ a i = some m)).card : ℝ) /
        (((Finset.Icc 1 n).filter (fun i ↦ a i = some (-m))).card : ℝ))
      (nhds 1) := by
  sorry

end OeisA153330

findings.description: The conclusion `∃ x y : ℕ, v.natAbs = 5 * x + 8 * y` adds a same-sign restriction on the integer coefficients that OEIS does not state. This changes the representation predicate, rather than merely rephrasing it: every integer v equals 5*(-3*v) + 8*(2*v), whereas, for example, |2| cannot equal 5*x + 8*y with natural x,y. Both facts were proved in the scratch file. The source's exceptions and examples make the intended same-sign interpretation plausible, so this is a defensible but unconfirmed strengthening—not an established equivalent formulation. The docstring's assertion that 'integers' means coefficients of the same sign needs source support.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A153330, Ya-Ping Lu's May 04 2024 comment: 'Except 1, 3 and 6, all terms can be written as 5x + 8y, where x and y are integers. For example, 62 = 5*6 + 8*4 and -101 = 5*(-9) + 8*(-7).' There is no explicit same-sign condition. Read at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A153/A153330.seq (canonical entry https://oeis.org/A153330).
findings.suggested_fix: Obtain and cite clarification that the coefficients must have the same sign. Otherwise, the literal conclusion is `∃ x y : ℤ, v = 5 * x + 8 * y`, which is trivial; present the current nonnegative-coefficient assertion separately as a proposed strengthened interpretation, rather than attributing the added restriction to OEIS.

findings.description: Quantifying over `m : ℤ` makes the four stated exceptions ineffective. Values -1, -3, -6 and -16 satisfy `hm`, and the ratio at -m is the reciprocal of the ratio at m. Consequently, convergence to 1 at either sign is equivalent to convergence to 1 at the other. I proved in Lean that the universally quantified statement with the current exclusions is equivalent to the statement with no exclusions at all. The source's exception list suggests that m may denote a nonnegative magnitude, but the source does not explicitly specify its domain; this choice therefore needs clarification rather than an unconditional misformalization verdict.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A153330, the same May 04 2024 comment: 'The ratio of the number of terms with the value of m to that of -m approaches 1 as n tends to infinity, where m != 1, 3, 6, or 16.' The preceding Conjecture 2 singles out those four positive values by their exceptional occurrence counts. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A153/A153330.seq
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify the intended domain of m. If the exceptions concern magnitudes, quantify over natural/positive m, casting to ℤ before negation, or retain integer m and exclude `m.natAbs ∈ {1, 3, 6, 16}`. Do not assert that the source explicitly gives either domain without additional evidence.

could_not_verify: OeisA153330.a on hypothetical nonterminating inputs: A153330 says that finiteness of all its elements is equivalent to the Collatz conjecture, supporting a partial stopping-time interpretation. However, its formula cites A006577, whose definition explicitly assigns -1 when 1 is never reached. Subtracting those sentinel values is not the same as propagating `none`, as Lean does. The two source descriptions do not settle which extension is intended; agreement on terminating inputs was verified.
review.notes: Reviewed all 13 declarations. The stopping-time calculations on terminating inputs and integer subtraction agree with all 10,000 b-file entries; the five existing tests are correct. Additional Lean proofs verify a(5)=3, a(8)=16 and a(12)=0. The proportions in Conjecture 1 lie in [0,1], so neither its n=0 quotient nor conditional-completeness defaults cause a problem. The m=0 case of Conjecture 4 is also harmless and was proved. No discrepancy was found in Conjectures 1 or 2 under the stated partial stopping-time convention. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles, and the review proofs do not depend on sorryAx. A further consistency check proves that the written, strengthened Conjecture 3 implies failure of Conjecture 4 at m=2; this is not an independent disproof of the original OEIS conjectures. The source records no resolution of the four conjectures.
